title: Window Flashing Sequence Explorer
description: Students will sequence (Bloom Level 3, Apply) the flashing steps around a window opening and will evaluate (Bloom Level 5, Evaluate) a flashing detail by tracing where water goes when a lap is reversed.
creator: The Science of the Built Environment
author: Dan McCreary
subject: The Science of the Built Environment
chapter_title: Cladding, Windows, Doors, and Air Sealing

prerequisites: The shingle principle for shedding water

pedagogical.learningObjective: Sequence the flashing steps around a window opening, and evaluate a detail by tracing where water goes when a lap is reversed.
recommendedUsage: In Build mode, press Next step and Previous step to add or remove the five layers in the correct order: sill pan, window, jamb tape, head flashing, and a weather-resistive barrier (WRB) lapped over the head flashing. Read the step text under the drawing.
Hover over any layer, or over a step chip, to see what it laps over. Click a layer to lift it away from the wall in an exploded view; click it again to put it back.

Press Pour water. Water runs down the wall in the elevation and the section. A green dot means water exits to the outside; a red circle with an X marks a leak. Try it with only some of the steps installed.
Tick Reverse a lap to tuck the barrier under the head flashing, then pour water and trace where the water goes.
Switch to Test the sequence, drag the five shuffled layers into slots 1 to 5, and read the hint if a slot is wrong. Correct layers build the wall as you go.
activities: Warm-up (5 min): Students write down the order they think the five layers go in, then step through Build mode to check it against the chapter's worked example.
Explore (10 min): Students press Pour water after each step and record which step first keeps water out of the opening at the head, the jambs, and the sill.
Evaluate (10 min): Students tick Reverse a lap, trace the water path, and explain in two sentences why the barrier must lap over the head flashing, using the shingle principle.
assessment: Students complete Test the sequence twice without hints and sketch the section from memory, labeling what each layer laps over.
Students explain why a bead of caulk across the top of a window is not a substitute for a head flashing.
